moduleTitle: Module 5. Renal, Digestive, Metabolic, Immune and Reproductive Physiology
topicSummary: Acid Base and Fluid Balance. 7 competencies, week 13.

competencies.name: Buffer systems
competencies.can: Compare the bicarbonate, phosphate, and protein buffer systems by location and speed and explain why bicarbonate is the dominant extracellular buffer.

competencies.name: Respiratory control of pH
competencies.can: Explain how a change in ventilation shifts the carbon dioxide and bicarbonate equilibrium and therefore plasma pH.

competencies.name: Renal control of pH
competencies.can: Describe how the kidney secretes hydrogen ion and reclaims or generates bicarbonate and explain why renal compensation is slower and more complete than respiratory compensation.

competencies.name: The four acid base disorders
competencies.can: Classify a disorder as respiratory or metabolic and as acidosis or alkalosis from pH, partial pressure of carbon dioxide, and bicarbonate.

competencies.name: Compensation
competencies.can: Determine whether an acid base disorder is uncompensated, partially compensated, or fully compensated and name the system doing the compensating.

competencies.name: Arterial blood gas interpretation
competencies.can: Interpret a set of arterial blood gas values and match the result to a plausible clinical cause.

competencies.name: Volume and osmolarity disturbances
competencies.can: Classify a disturbance as volume depletion or overload and as hypoosmotic, isosmotic, or hyperosmotic and predict the resulting fluid shift between compartments.
